To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a dual sensor system can be used to measure POA solar irradiance with a spectral response that closely matches that of any PV module.
the spectral response of the reference cell is the most important parameter in determining the accuracy of performance ratio calculations.
• A spectrally selective reference cell is not necessary to monitor the performance of a PV system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a spectrally selective sensor for PV system monitoring.
improving the accuracy of POA irradiance measurements for the purpose of improving PV system performance monitoring.
the development and evaluation of spectrally selective sensors that can be used in PV performance monitoring systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed dual sensor method provides a cost effective alternative to using a reference cell for monitoring c-Si PV modules.
the proposed method is a viable alternative for POA irradiance monitoring in PV systems and can be used for monitoring and fault detection.

the spectral mismatch between a reference cell and a photovoltaic cell (PV cell) can be compensated by using a dual-sensor approach that combines the output signals from two different types of spectrally selective sensors to produce a composite output signal that closely approximates the response of the PV cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a spectrally selective sensor is a practical solution for measuring POA for all types of solar PV systems.

the spectral mismatch between the reference cell and the PV module is a major source of uncertainty in the determination of POA irradiance for thin-film PV modules and the spectral response of the reference cell should be tailored to the spectral response of thin-film PV cells.
we are working on a new method to measure irradiance that is more spectrally and directionally selective than pyranometers and more spectrally matched to PV modules than reference cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spectral selectivity of a PV system monitoring sensor is more important than its absolute accuracy.
the spectral selectivity of the sensor can be used to improve the accuracy of POA irradiance measurements and, in turn, improve the accuracy of the performance ratio.
the use of dual-sensor systems can be used to improve the accuracy of performance monitoring systems and to reduce the cost of PV system maintenance.
